courierSpeed.note: An aide riding across country, about 300 m/min. No source found.

courierLossChance.note: Chance a courier is killed, lost or misdirected. A lost order is sent again after resendTime.

resendTime.note: Delay before the sender realises an order has not arrived and repeats it.

delayJitter.note: Staff delays vary by plus or minus this fraction.

staffDelayArmy.note: Time for an army or corps headquarters to write and dispatch an order. Accounts in Muir suggest minutes; the figure is a guess.

staffDelayDivision.note: Time for a division commander to read an order and pass it on.

staffDelayBrigade.note: Time for a brigadier to set his battalions in motion.

radiusArmy.note: Default command radius; a scenario may set its own per commander.

radiusBrigade.note: Covers four battalions in line with intervals, about 750 m of front.

initiativeDefault.note: Chance that a commander who sees a reason to act on his own does so at each check.

initiativeInterval.note: How often a commander reviews the situation.

commanderSpeed.note: A mounted commander keeping station on his formation.

brigadierBehind.note: A brigadier rides this far behind the centre of his formed units.

generalBehind.note: A division or corps commander rides this far behind the centre of his subordinates.

engageRadius.note: A unit marching on an objective turns to fight when formed enemy is this close.

arriveDistance.note: A unit within this distance of its ordered position has arrived.

supportDistance.note: A supporting formation keeps this far behind the one it supports.

withdrawDistance.note: Distance fallen back on a withdraw order that names no place.

restrainedLeash.note: Cavalry held in reserve, on hold, moving or in support looks for targets only within this fraction of its usual distance.

outOfCommandRecovery.note: Morale recovery of a formed unit outside every command radius in its chain.

rallyCommanderFactor.note: Morale recovery of a routed unit inside the radius of a commander in its chain.

shakenMorale.note: A formed unit below this counts as shaken when a commander reviews his formation.

stallFraction.note: An attacking commander may halt to regroup when more than this share of his formed units is shaken.

regroupTime.note: Length of such a halt before the attack resumes.

collapseFraction.note: A commander may pull back when this share of his units has routed or gone.

opportunityRangeInfantry.note: An infantry commander not ordered to attack may counter-attack a vulnerable enemy this close to his formation.

opportunityRangeCavalry.note: The same for a cavalry commander.

opportunityMorale.note: An enemy below this, or changing formation, or in melee, counts as vulnerable. Same threshold the prototype uses for a bayonet charge.

counterattackTime.note: A counter-attack made on a commander's own initiative lasts this long, then his previous orders resume.

commanderRiskRange.note: A commander is at risk while formed enemy is within this distance of him.

commanderRiskPerSecond.note: About 1.2% a minute while at risk. General officers fell often in this period; the rate is a guess.

commanderDownShock.note: Lost by formed units of his command within his radius, multiplied by steadiness.

successionTime.note: Time before the next senior officer takes over. Until then the formation is out of command.

successorInitiative.note: A successor's initiative relative to the man he replaces.

successorRadius.note: A successor's command radius relative to the man he replaces.

autoBrigadeSize.note: When a scenario gives no command structure, infantry is grouped into brigades of this many battalions.
